content:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio drew some attention for his demeanor during President Donald Trump’s Friday press conference, even as the secretary later stepped up to defend the president’s recent trip to China.

Trump returned to Washington on Thursday after his historic meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping. The meeting produced a four-point “Declaration toward Peace,” but did not appear to yield breakthroughs on the Russia-Ukraine war or the war with Iran. Ahead of the briefing, Trump told followers on Truth Social that he would discuss the three-leader meeting alongside trade deals with Thailand and the Philippines.

Vice President JD Vance and Rubio stood behind Trump at the podium while he spoke to the press in the White House Briefing Room.

“Marco Rubio is dying a slow death up there,” one X user wrote. “Marco Rubio looks like he would like to be anywhere but here,” another said.

Body language experts who watched clips from the remarks noted that Rubio appeared visibly uneasy.

“There’s just repeated shifting, subtle rocking of his body, a micro shoulder shrug, an upward jut of the chin and tightening at the corners of his mouth,” body language expert Susan Constantine said. “Individually, these gestures tell us very little, but collectively, they suggested heightened physical activation.”

Abbie Maroño, a behavioral scientist, pointed to Rubio’s eye movement.

“His gaze repeatedly darts around the room … rather than maintaining sustained visual attention toward Trump while he is speaking,” she said.

Maroño added that the pattern can be consistent with heightened vigilance or unease, and that the frequency and restlessness of the movements matter here, not the looking away itself.

There is no specific indicator that suggests Rubio is reacting to Trump in the moment, Maroño added, and it’s unclear what might be causing any discomfort.

“We can clearly see he is not present,” Maroño said.

Traci Brown, who studies body language and behavior, pointed out that while Vance smiles as Trump jokes about the Nobel Peace Prize, Rubio doesn’t.

“Instead, his knees break and he dips,” Brown said, which she reads as disengagement.

Rubio and Vance shared a brief, perplexed look and smile behind the president after Trump remarked on his own genetics while discussing MIT.

“I have great knowledge of MIT because a member of my family spent his life at MIT, as who they say is now the greatest professor in the history of MIT. So I have a great understanding of — I guess, maybe genetically I’m blessed,” Trump said.

Rubio later stepped up to the podium to push back against critics who questioned why Trump met with Putin and Xi.

“These three countries, the United States, Russia and China … possess the overwhelming majority of nuclear weapons on this planet,” he said. “The idea that these three leaders should not engage on a regular basis is not just absurd, it’s dangerous.”

“The better these three leaders get along, the easier and more conducive the environment will be to actually agree to things that are concrete down the road,” he continued.

Rubio’s defense came after Trump praised his own relationship with Putin during the press conference. When asked if he believes Russia to be “a friend to America,” Trump said, “I can’t speak to America,” but “I consider him to be somebody that I have a very good relationship, and it’s actually very good.”

After White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller spoke, Trump concluded the briefing by joking that Miller was “better than these two guys,” gesturing to Rubio and Vance, before asking Miller, “Do you want to run for president?”

The State Department responded to HuffPost’s inquiries with a statement:

“These ‘reporters’ clearly are experiencing some sort of cognitive malfunction,” it said. “Secretary Rubio is a human who moves and has expressions, as we all do. Thank you for your attention to this matter.”
